incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), as amended, including Articles 6, 7, 17, 101, 128, 153, 154, 156, 172, 192, 208, 228, 412, and 419; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 7, 8, 10, and 11; Company Registration Approval Rules; and the MOEA Guidance on Registration of Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration Division, with local filing accepted at the MOEA Central Region Service Office or via the MOEA One-Stop Online Application Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration and Certificate of Incorporation filed under Article 419 of the Taiwan Company Act, together with the foreign investment approval and the CPA capital verification report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability company, and no blocked escrow account is mandatorily prescribed. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the Investment Commission of the MOEA requires the full approved foreign investment amount to be remitted to Taiwan in New Taiwan Dollars and deposited into a temporary bank account in the Company name before the final registration certificate is issued. The bank will hold these funds without release until the CPA capital verification report is submitted and the company registration is approved, unless a written release is obtained from the foreign exchange bank based on the investment approval letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD (THE COMPANY) ADOPTED ON THIS DATE PURSUANT TO THE TAIWAN COMPANY ACT, THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION OF THE COMPANY, AND THE STATUTE FOR INVESTMENT BY FOREIGN NATIONALS. WHEREAS, the Company is being formed as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company in Taiwan for the purpose of providing global App Store optimization, multilingual organic search, and localization agency services; and WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to approve the initial corporate, financial, and administrative arrangements of the Company; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-UP CAPITAL. The Board acknowledges the subscription of the entire issued share capital by the sole shareholder and directs the Chairperson to collect the fully paid-up capital equal to the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The Chairperson is further directed to deposit such capital into a separate temporary bank account established in the name of the Company, to obtain a bank-issued capital certificate and foreign exchange receipt, and to engage a certified public accountant to issue the capital verification report required for registration. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board approves the opening of the Company principal operating bank account with a financial institution licensed in Taiwan. The Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly in any two of them, are hereby authorized to open, operate, sign for, and close any bank account of the Company, to execute banking instructions and payment transfers, to apply for online banking credentials, and to approve foreign currency settlements relevant to cross-border service revenue. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at its principal place of business in Taiwan, namely the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and directs the Company Secretary to file the registered office address with the competent registry authority, to display the statutory corporate signboard at such location, and to notify the National Taxation Bureau of the office address for tax registration purposes. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints the following officers for terms expiring at the next annual general meeting: one Director and Chairperson, one General Manager, one Chief Financial Officer, and one Company Secretary. Each officer shall have the powers and duties prescribed by law and the Articles of Incorporation, and shall represent the Company before all public and private authorities within the lawful scope of the Company business. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. The Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Company Secretary, acting jointly in any two of them, are authorized to execute, notarize, file, and submit all incorporation documents, foreign exchange forms, tax registrations, business permits, and other instruments required to implement these resolutions. RESOLVED FURTHER, that these resolutions shall take effect immediately upon adoption and shall be recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of the Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC) and MOEA One-Stop Online Application Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the foreign investment application under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, identifying the ultimate beneficial owner, the paid-up capital amount in New Taiwan Dollars, and the remittance bank. Simultaneously reserve the proposed Chinese and English company names on the MOEA One-Stop Online Application Portal to confirm that the name is not identical to an existing registered company. The application must include notarized certificates of incorporation and good standing of the foreign parent company, a power of attorney authenticated by a notary public, the precise business scope covering ASO, SEO, and localization agency services, and a capital remittance plan. After approval, the Investment Commission will issue a foreign investment approval letter; this letter must be included in the later company registration filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
Certificate of good standing issued by the shareholder home registry
Power of attorney in favor of the local filing agent
Business scope description in English and Chinese
Passport or corporate ID copy of the responsible officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the applicant must respond to the Investment Commission within fourteen calendar days with clarifying documents, including proof of source of funds and shareholder resolution. If the company name reservation is rejected due to conflict, the applicant may file a new name reservation request within five business days. A formal appeal may be lodged with the Executive Yuan within thirty days after a final adverse decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization, and Execution of Articles and Officer Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary public or overseas Taiwan representative office; MOEA Company Registration Portal for electronic signature upload
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Chinese, covering the company name, capital structure, business scope, registered office, number of directors, and appointment rules. Execute the articles before the founding shareholder and ensure that all signatures are notarized or legalized according to the place of execution. Prepare the consent letters for the appointment of the Chairperson, General Manager, Chief Financial Officer, and Company Secretary, together with each officer valid identification document and residency proof. After execution, upload the notarized articles and appointment consents to the MOEA Company Registration Portal using the electronic certificate of the responsible person. The business scope must match the Investment Commission approval exactly and may include App Store optimization, multilingual SEO, and localization consulting services.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Chinese
English translation of the Articles of Incorporation
Consent letters of all appointed officers
Proof of residence of the registered office (lease agreement or title deed)
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA rejects or suspends the notarized documents, the company shall receive a written deficiency notice identifying the missing or non-conforming items. The company must correct the documents and re-submit them through the portal within fifteen days. If the deficiency is based on the business scope, the company must first apply for a supplemental investment approval from the Investment Commission before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Escrow Deposit, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), authorized foreign exchange bank, and certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Remit the approved paid-up capital from the foreign shareholder bank account to Taiwan through a designated foreign exchange bank. The remittance instruction must reference the foreign investment approval letter number, the exact company name, and the purpose code for direct investment. After the funds arrive, instruct the receiver bank to issue a foreign exchange receipt and a capital remittance certificate. Open a temporary bank account in the name of the Company at the receiving bank, deposit the entire remitted amount into that account, and request a bank-issued balance certificate. Deliver the balance certificate to a certified public accountant, who will prepare a CPA capital verification report confirming that the paid-up capital has been fully subscribed and deposited and is under the exclusive control of the Company. The CPA report must be dated no earlier than fifteen days before the company registration filing.
required_dossiers: Foreign exchange receipt issued by the receiving bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Central Bank or the foreign exchange bank questions the remittance, the company must provide additional evidence of lawful source of funds, including audited financial statements of the foreign shareholder and bank statements. A rejected remittance may be reversed and resubmitted after corrective documentation is filed. If the CPA report contains discrepancies, the CPA must issue a supplemental report and the capital may need to be redeposited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final Incorporation Registration and Issuance of Company Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration Division, Central Region Service Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the final incorporation registration application on the MOEA One-Stop Online Application Portal. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, CPA capital verification report, foreign investment approval letter, officer consents, identification documents, registered office proof, and temporary bank account certificate. Pay the official filing fee through the online payment gateway and retain the payment receipt. The MOEA reviews the filing for statutory compliance, capital verification, and name conformity. Upon approval, the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate and automatically notifies the National Taxation Bureau, which assigns the unified business taxation number (GUI number). The company may then collect the registration certificate in person or receive it by registered mail, and must complete VAT registration and unemployment insurance registration within fifteen days.
required_dossiers: Bank capital certificate and foreign exchange receipt
Consent letters and IDs of officers
Online payment receipt for filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a suspension notice, the company has thirty days to cure the stated deficiencies and re-submit the amended documents. A rejected application may be appealed to the MOEA within thirty days under the Administrative Appeal Act. If the GUI number is not automatically generated, the company may file a separate tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau using the MOEA approval letter and the registration certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the ASO/SEO localization agency is a pure digital services and consulting business under ISIC 7310, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no mandatory industrial or manufacturing operating license is required under Taiwan law for the stated scope of global App Store optimization, multilingual organic search, and localization agency services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - this office-based digital agency engages in no industrial activity requiring approval from the Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is required; the company does not fall within any statutory EIA category because it performs no resource extraction, manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company generates no measurable wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous waste. Office waste is limited to general domestic refuse and must be disposed of through the local municipal collection system. The company must still comply with the Waste Disposal Act for any administrative paper documents and electronic records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial fire safety certification. As a leased office premises, the company shall ensure compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, maintain a basic first aid kit and fire extinguisher as required by the local fire department, and display the business tax certificate. A fire safety inspection for the leasehold office may be requested by the landlord, but no separate civil defense permit or structural load inspection is required for the licensing agency business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (Republic of China) - Tax Administration, operating through the National Taxation Bureaus; electronic portal: Ministry of Finance Tax e-Filing Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw) and e-Invoice Integration Service Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first complete the legal registration of its Taiwan branch or business unit with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain the branch establishment approval. Immediately after that legal registration, the foreign parent must apply to the competent National Taxation Bureau for tax registration, submitting the following statutory documentation: certified certificate of foreign incorporation or registration, articles of incorporation and company charter, approved Taiwan branch registration, power of attorney and identification of the Taiwan responsible person, proof of Taiwan business premises, and the Taxable Business Registration Application. The National Taxation Bureau will verify the information, register the foreign taxpayer in the Taiwan tax ledger, and assign an eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBN), which serves as both the Taiwan Tax Identification Number and the VAT registration number. Foreign e-commerce and digital service providers with no fixed Taiwan place of business may instead complete the simplified cross-border electronic services tax registration on the Ministry of Finance e-Tax portal, obtaining a Taiwan VAT registration identity without establishing a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a registered Taiwan branch or limited-liability subsidiary is taxed as a separate corporate taxpayer on Taiwan-source income, and no pass-through treatment is available to the foreign parent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Taiwan Income Tax Act and the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act do not provide check-the-box elections, hybrid mismatch elections, or entity classification elections. The foreign investor chooses initially between a Taiwan branch and a Taiwan subsidiary, and that tax classification is permanent for the taxpayer entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taiwan Business Tax, formally the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Under the Business Tax Act, any person making taxable sales in Taiwan must register for Business Tax before commencing operations. The general VAT and Uniform Invoice registration regime becomes mandatory when average monthly sales equal or exceed NT$80,000; small-scale operators below that threshold are assessed at a deemed rate. For foreign e-commerce and digital service providers selling B2C digital services into Taiwan, registration is mandatory once annual taxable digital service sales exceed NT$480,000; B2B digital services are subject to reverse-charge by the Taiwanese business recipient and carry no seller registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates Uniform Invoice issuance through certified electronic systems. Registered VAT operators must use the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Integration Service Platform and transmit invoice data via API or Turnkey connections within statutory upload windows, with near-real-time transmission required for cloud invoices. The platform validates each invoice, assigns the national invoice number and an anti-counterfeiting digital verification code, and records cancellations or amendments electronically. Failure to transmit timely is legally treated as failure to issue a Uniform Invoice and is penalized under the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 9 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, goods exported outside Taiwan customs territory and services supplied to and consumed by a non-Taiwan customer are eligible for the 0% VAT rate. For goods, the exporter must prove physical movement through customs with an export declaration and transport document. For qualifying offshore digital services, the service must be rendered to a foreign business or individual, the beneficial use and enjoyment must occur outside Taiwan, and the consideration must be received in foreign exchange and repatriated through authorized banking channels. Digital services supplied to Taiwan customers or consumed in Taiwan remain taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) serving as the statutory export Bill of Entry, filed electronically with the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing that the goods physically left Taiwan customs jurisdiction
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export sales contract addressed to the foreign customer
Foreign exchange repatriation evidence: inward remittance certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange settlement certificate from an authorized Taiwan banking channel

For digital/ASO/SEO services: signed service agreement, service delivery log, IP/location evidence, and a written statement confirming the service was used outside Taiwan, plus the foreign customer's business or VAT registration proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan customs and tax authorities cross-match export declarations, shipping manifests, foreign exchange receipts, and invoice data. If zero-rating is claimed without the complete export, delivery, and foreign-exchange evidence, the supply is reclassified as domestic, VAT is assessed at 5%, input tax refunds are suspended, and the taxpayer must repay any previously refunded VAT. The Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act authorizes a penalty up to five times the underpaid tax for false zero-rating claims. Forged bills of lading, fictitious FIRCs, false service-use statements, or intentional omission are subject to criminal liability under the Tax Evasion Act and the Customs Penalty Act, with back-assessment up to seven years plus statutory interest from the original due date.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days_: The 180-day deadline applies from the date of export or service performance; if foreign exchange is not received within the deadline, the zero-rating documentation bundle is deemed incomplete unless formal statutory deferral is granted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC) as the primary foreign exchange and monetary authority for Taiwan; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China for all onshore CNY capital account and trade-related foreign exchange administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates under a managed floating exchange rate with current account convertibility broadly unrestricted. Legal-entity current account receipts and payments, including service fees from app store optimization and localization work, may be freely transacted through Authorized Foreign Exchange Banks, subject to prescribed remittance declaration thresholds. Capital account transactions, including inbound capital injection into a Taiwan-registered entity, foreign investor equity, or repatriation of sale proceeds, remain under CBC oversight and require supporting documentation such as investment approval, audited financial statements, and shareholder resolutions. Taiwan does not mandate surrender of export proceeds; receipts may remain in foreign-currency deposit accounts. Profit remittance by foreign shareholders is permitted after tax clearance and compliance with CBC settlement rules. Mainland China, by contrast, maintains stricter convertibility controls through SAFE. A Chinese WFOE must register an FDI enterprise with SAFE to open a capital account, and every injection must be verified against the FDI registration. Current account items such as payments for advertising services are convertible after genuine transaction verification, but funds cannot be diverted to equity investment or prohibited uses. Repatriation of profits from the WFOE requires an audited statutory financial report, tax completion certificate, board resolution on profit distribution, and bank verification. The asymmetry between Taiwan and China creates structural friction, especially for TWD app-store settlements flowing into a CNY entity; funds must first be collected by a Taiwan operating account, reflected in service invoices, and then settled through SAFE-monitored trade or service transaction rails. Round-tripping, over-invoicing, and mismatched payment purpose codes are major regulatory exposure points for an ASO and SEO localization agency dealing with many small-batch digital advertising payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not impose mandatory surrender of export or service export proceeds. Exporters and service providers may retain foreign currency proceeds in foreign currency deposit accounts or convert them voluntarily. Export receipts should be collected within 180 days of shipment or service completion unless extended with CBC approval. For Mainland China, SAFE also does not require forced surrender; eligible trade and service exports can be settled by authorized banks through the goods and services trade monitoring system. In both regimes, the carrier bank is responsible for verifying underlying transaction documents and assigning the correct foreign exchange purpose code before settlement or crediting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Deposit Account / NTD Operational Settlement Account
Corporate Multi-Currency Account / Trust and Clearing Account
NTD Current Account / USD Deposit Account for advertising settlement
CNY Clearing Account / Cross-Strait Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs, including Wise B2B and Payoneer, are not licensed as deposit-taking banks in Taiwan and cannot serve as the primary corporate treasury account or statutory capital escrow depository. They are viable only as supplementary payment facilitators routed through licensed Taiwan banks or partner financial institutions, and their use is further constrained in Mainland China where WFOE capital and trade settlements must pass through SAFE-regulated onshore bank accounts. The overall viability is low as a stand-alone banking solution and medium only for low-value cross-border app-store commission payouts under a sponsoring bank arrangement. Heavy reliance on EMIs creates upstream KYC opacity, sanctions screening gaps, and potential frozen-funds exposure during account reviews, so a Tier-1 domestic bank relationship must remain the operational backbone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Taiwan, the statutory director and beneficial owner generally must appear physically at the bank branch for corporate account opening, or provide a notarized power of attorney with the appointed officer attending in person. Remote opening is not routinely permitted for the first corporate account. Foreign corporate documents must be notarized and authenticated through the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in the jurisdiction of incorporation. For the Chinese WFOE, the legal representative must also appear in person at an authorized bank for capital account activation; some onshore banks allow video verification for ordinary operational accounts, but SAFE-related capital account signing and FX business establishment require a physical or formally notarized appointment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity because the WFOE parent is ultimately controlled through a complex cross-strait holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated corporate registry chart from the Cayman/BVI or Hong Kong holding entity if applicable, full share ownership cascade up to natural persons, passport and national identity documentation for all UBOs holding more than 10 percent, trust deeds or including declarations for any nominee share arrangements, and a source-of-wealth statement signed by the ultimate parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity small-value remittances to less-regulated app developers, influencer banks, and pay-per-install networks without clear contractual linkage to the ASO and SEO commercial model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed service agreements with every app store, ad network, influencer, or localization subcontractor, batch remittance purpose schedules, monthly campaign delivery reports with app-market listing URLs, keyword ranking screenshots, platform dashboards from Apple, Google, or Meta, and evidence that the payment counterparty actually performed the localized advertising service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected round-tripping or over-invoicing in cross-strait flows between TWD-denominated Taiwan receipts and CNY-denominated WFOE distribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ACPA-certified or CPA-audited transfer pricing documentation, benchmark study comparing the ASO agency margins, intercompany service agreement between the Taiwan principal and the CN WFOE, SAFE FDI Registration Certificate for inbound investment, tax filing proof showing the declared service revenue, and detailed invoices tied to specific keyword coverage and localization milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or government-entity exposure from app store promotion or organic search optimization touching China, Taiwan, and other high-scrutiny jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening results for all counterparty counterparties, corporate certificates confirming no politically exposed persons controlling the beneficiary accounts, foreign policy or national-security screening opinion from the bank compliance team, advertising content archives proving lawful digital marketing services, and a written AML compliance manual plus annual independent training record for the agency.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the CN WFOE must be injected through the SAFE-registered FDI capital account using a proper SWIFT MT103 remittance from the Taiwan parent, with the payment purpose code described as foreign direct investment capital injection. The remitting bank in Taiwan must classify the outward transfer under CBC capital account reporting and retain the board resolution, FDI registration certificate of the Chinese WFOE, share subscription agreement, and formulaic capital verification report. Upon receipt, the Chinese settlement bank will verify the SAFE business registration and require the enterprise to submit a capital account statement within ten business days. The Taiwan-origin funds cannot enter through Wise B2B, Payoneer, or any other EMI unless the carrying bank is a licensed AFEB and SAFE data exchange is completed. For profit distribution, the WFOE must complete the annual statutory audit, file tax returns, obtain the profit distribution board resolution, and then apply for TWD or USD remittance through the designated onshore bank using the current account purpose code for profit remittance by foreign investors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for ASO and SEO localization should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor payments, with proper purpose codes such as advertising agency services, software licensing, or localization consultancy. Commercial documentary letters of credit are appropriate for sizable software development or translation vendor contracts where performance and shipping documents are verifiable. Documentary collections may be used for smaller localization service trades, but the bank should always have the underlying service contract, invoice, delivery acceptance report, and proof of regulatory licensing in the destination market. For Apple, Google, and other app-store developer payments, the rake-off should be made from a Taiwan-operated bank account or a dedicated commercial card linked to the Tier-1 bank, with the corresponding transaction feed retained for anti-layering review. Wise B2B and Payoneer should only be used for low-value test payments and never as a substitute for a SWIFT-cleared vendor payment when the purpose code is capital or large service trade.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruements: Onshore CNY/USD or TWD/USD deliverable forward contracts with the settlement bank, backed by documented service trade exposure for the ASO and SEO agency revenue stream
Cross-currency swaps between CNY, TWD, and USD to hedge long-dated localization contracts, limited to notional principal supported by signed client or vendor agreements
Forward option structures allowed by CBC/SAFE with strictly non-speculative intent and real transaction evidence

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where legally permitted and booked through an authorized bank with a clear offshore/onshore price reference, generally used by foreign counterparties rather than the local entity as principal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 31 of the year following the taxable year for calendar-year filers; one-month extension available when the return is filed by a licensed tax agent on behalf of the company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax, capped at 20%; after statutory demand, tax authority may assess income by estimation; unpaid tax accrues interest at the postal two-year fixed deposit rate; additional fines apply under Articles 108 and 110 of the Income Tax Act, and persistent non-filing may lead to compulsory restriction on corporate banking operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) resolution and audited financial statements filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Central Competent Authority via the National Business Registration Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held no later than June 30 for calendar-year companies; audited financial statements must be submitted to MOEA within 15 days after shareholder approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within the deadline may result in fines of NT$20,000 to NT$1,000,000 under the Company Act; non-filing of the audited financial statements with MOEA leads to administrative correction orders, fines of up to NT$500,000, and negative impact on foreign investment registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (ROC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year companies, due March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file timely may trigger suspension or revocation of the foreign investment approval, administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Act, and difficulties with future capital repatriation, dividends remittance, or expansion applications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Company Registry Declaration (Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the AGM (no later than July 30 for calendar-year companies); event-driven changes must be reported within 30 days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual UBO confirmation may lead to administrative warnings, fines of up to NT$500,000 under Articles 387 and 388 of the Company Act, civil liability for actions of unauthorized persons, and repeat violations can result in an application for judicial dissolution or company strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent CPA statutory audit is mandatory under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the Business Entity Accounting Act if: (a) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million; (b) the entity has issued public securities or is regulated by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC); (c) the entity is designated by MOEA/FSC as requiring audit by reason of industry, scale, or foreign investment sensitivity; or (d) the parent or guarantor is a public or oversea-listed enterprise demanding consolidated group audit. Even below NT$30 million capital, if annual revenue exceeds NT$100 million or headcount exceeds 100, the tax authority may require the submission of CPA-audited financial statements. For a WFOE engaged in digital advertising and app localization services, the Investment Commission will generally request an audit qualification once the entity reaches the NT$30 million capital threshold or when operational scale indicates reliable financial reporting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS) is applicable for entities under FSC supervision; non-public enterprises may apply Taiwan GAAP / Business Entity Accounting Standards (SME Accounting Standards) as codified by the Business Entity Accounting Act and the MOEA's Regulations Governing the Preparation of Financial Reports. For tax filing purposes, the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return requires reconciliation between the financial statements prepared under the governing accounting framework and the Income Tax Act adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain an internal beneficial ownership register reflecting the ultimate natural persons who directly or indirectly control 25% or more of the shares or voting rights, pursuant to the Money Laundering Control Act and Company Act Article 14-1. This register is filed with MOEA at incorporation and updated within 30 calendar days of any shareholding or control change. Annually, concurrently with the AGM and audited financial statement submission, the company must confirm in the MOEA company registration portal that the UBO data is current as of the AGM date. The annual corporate income tax filing is cross-referenced with the shareholder and UBO data; failure to maintain accurate UBO records may invalidate certain shareholder resolutions and attract administrative and penal sanctions. The 30-day reporting window for share transfers also applies to any change in directors, supervisors, or corporate representatives.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified WFOEs may access the 5-year tax holiday for encouraged industries under the Grand Canal New Area and other state-level new zones, reduced 15% preferential rate for encouraged hi-tech and integrated circuit enterprises, super-deduction of 100% on qualifying R&D expenses, and additional 50% super-deduction on wages of disabled employees; no general patent box regime is available, but technology transfer income up to RMB 5 million is exempt and 50% of the excess may be exempt; free-zone preferential rates are only available in Hainan Free Trade Port (15%) and certain encouraged industries in the Western Regions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) Return Form A010000 (中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类）) filed via the State Taxation Administration’s e-Tax System (电子税务局); non-resident WFOE filers complete schedules A100000 (main return), A105000, and related supplementary tables.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: EIT annual return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., May 31); quarterly provisional payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter, with annual reconciliation and final payment by May 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue (营业收入) – gross revenue from ASO/SEO localization services, app-store optimization subscriptions, and performance-based growth fees, excluding VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law matching ASC 606 / IFRS 15 timing; repatriated management fees, rechargeable costs, or recharged marketing expenses to a foreign parent must be excluded unless supported by a valid service contract and economic substance documentation; if revenue is derived from PRC-source services, the full gross amount must be reported even if billing is made by the offshore group company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating cost (营业成本) – direct costs of localization, translation, ASO keyword research, app-store metadata production, ad-creative production, and search engine optimization labor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border cost recharges from a related foreign entity are deductible only to the extent they satisfy the arm’s length standard and are supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; any global/group cost allocation charge that lacks a direct benefit test will be disallowed and reclassified as a non-deductible deemed dividend distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total selling expenses (销售费用) – sales commissions, overseas platform placement fees, digital advertising costs, and business development expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advertising fees paid to foreign related parties may be subject to 10% withholding tax as service fees or royalties if embedded in app-store placement or keyword licensing; ensure economic substance in China and avoid circular transactions where the WFOE merely passes through marketing costs to the Taiwan parent without a mark-up.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total administrative expenses (管理费用) – management, legal, accounting, office rental, and group management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Group management fees paid to the Taiwan head office or related offshore service company are deductible only when invoiced, supported by actual services, and not duplicative of shareholder costs; a pure ‘cost-plus’ allocation without local supervision or decision-making records will be treated as a non-deductible shareholder contribution or disguised dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total finance expenses (财务费用) – interest expense on shareholder loans, intercompany borrowings, bank charges, and foreign exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to Taiwanese or offshore related lenders is subject to 10% withholding tax, or 5% under the Cross-Strait Agreement if the beneficial owner is a Taiwan resident enterprise and a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate is obtained; thin capitalization rules limit deductible interest to 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for related-party loans and require a written loan agreement, commercial purpose, and actual fund flow.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit (利润总额) – accounting profit before tax computed in accordance with PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the starting point for tax reconciliation; any accounting profit recognized on transactions with the Taiwan parent that would not have occurred between independent enterprises must be adjusted upward; the annual anti-avoidance adjustment is made on Schedule A105000 and reflected here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation adjustments (纳税调整项目明细表) – add-back of non-deductible expenses, excess entertainment expenses, unverified related-party fees, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory reconciliation for all cross-border payments: amounts paid to foreign related parties exceeding the arm’s length price, withholding tax borne by the WFOE, and penalties or fines are added back; the taxpayer must prepare contemporaneous TP documentation to defend all intercompany charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax incentives and deductions (免税、减计收入及加计扣除优惠明细表) – R&D super-deduction, technology transfer exemption, and encouraged industry preferential rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: WFOE may claim the 100% R&D super-deduction on qualifying ASO/SEO algorithm research and localization software development; documentary requirements include a project plan, R&D personnel logs, financial accounting ledger, and contemporaneous technical documentation; a foreign-parent owned IP arrangement cannot transfer the R&D benefit to the WFOE unless the WFOE bears economic risk and controls the development.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit schedule (境外所得税收抵免) – not applicable to WFOE’s PRC-source income but relevant if the WFOE receives dividends or services income from Taiwan or other foreign sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan-sourced dividend or branch profit received by the PRC WFOE is subject to PRC EIT at 20% (reduced to 10% effectively if treaty-reduced) with a foreign tax credit for Taiwan income tax paid; only direct taxes are creditable and the credit is capped at the PRC tax attributable to that foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (应纳税所得额) and tax payable at 25% standard rate (or preferential 15%/20% rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise if its place of effective management is in China; the headline 25% statutory rate applies to the worldwide income unless a preferential rate is available; software companies with less than 21 employees or qualifying small low-profit enterprises may compute at 20% with reduced taxable income thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized RMB 2,000 per return with an additional RMB 2,000 per month or fraction-month (maximum RMB 20,000) under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Law; late payment attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax; fraudulent filing or omission of cross-border income exceeding RMB 50,000 may constitute tax evasion under Article 63, leading to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax, possible blacklisting of the legal representative, and criminal liability for the responsible person.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 3 and Article 37, assessed on gross dividends paid by the WFOE to its Taiwan corporate shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation (海峡两岸避免双重课税及加强税务合作协议) is the operative DTA: to claim the 5% reduced dividend withholding rate (or 10% if not qualifying), the Taiwan shareholder must (1) obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate (居住者證明) from the National Taxation Bureau and submit it to the PRC withholding agent before each payment or as required by the local STA; (2) provide a Form 2 / beneficial ownership self-declaration confirming that it is the ultimate beneficial owner of the dividend and not a conduit; (3) maintain shareholding of at least 25% in the PRC WFOE continuously for 365 days preceding the dividend distribution (if claiming the 5% qualified rate); (4) provide a notarized certificate of incorporation, articles of association, and board resolution approving the distribution; and (5) undergo the STA’s mutual agreement procedure (MAP) if the Taiwan authority refuses to accept the treaty benefit. Interest and royalties generally retain 10% PRC WHT, but the Cross-Strait Agreement reduces interest and royalty WHT to 5% if the beneficial owner is a Taiwan resident enterprise and the income is connected with a Taiwan permanent establishment; the same TRC and beneficial ownership evidence is mandatory; a special prior-taxation year-end review is recommended because Taiwan and PRC tax authorities have limited automatic exchange and may apply the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) to reject treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties for the use of IP, software copyright, algorithms, or app-store trademarks are subject to 10% PRC WHT plus VAT at 6% (if the foreign recipient is deemed a PRC VAT taxpayer); interest paid to a Taiwan lender is subject to 10% PRC WHT plus VAT on interest (financial services, generally 6% for foreign lenders); treaty-reduced rates: 5% royalty and interest WHT under the Cross-Strait Agreement when the Taiwan beneficial owner provides a TRC and meets the beneficial ownership test; a 0% rate is not available for interest with related parties unless a specific exemption applies under Notice 2018 No. 91 for qualified foreign lenders to a PRC subsidiary—which will rarely apply to a Taiwan parent; withholding at source is mandatory and the WFOE must report and pay the withheld tax to the STA within 7 days of payment or of the date the obligation arises.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The local file is mandatory when related-party transactions in a single category exceed RMB 40 million (or total related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million) in the annual tax year; the master file is required when total related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million and the group’s consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 5 billion; below these thresholds, the WFOE must still file the annual related-party transaction reporting form (同期资料/年度关联业务往来报告表) through the STA’s e-filing system, and a contemporaneous TP documentation file must be ready within the statutory deadline (by the filing date for local file, and within 30 days of the STA request for master file).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC applies the substance-over-form and general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) under EIT Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulation Article 120; a WFOE that merely invoices localization services without performing core functions—such as app-store optimization strategy, keyword research, translation quality control, and ad-buying decisions—will be recharacterized as a shell entity, its income may be reallocated to the Taiwan parent, and the cost-plus mark-up must reflect the risks borne and functions performed; the OECD BEPS Action 5 economic substance analysis is also relevant for any Taiwanese IP licensing structure; for the WFOE to qualify as the principal or limited-risk distributor/agent of the App Growth Agency, it must demonstrate local employees with technical competence, actual decision-making authority to bind the agency, payroll and social insurance records, tangible office premises, and a bank account through which client receipts flow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays the Taiwan parent a 'management fee', 'app-store API royalty', or 'marketing cost reimbursement' that is not supported by written contracts, actual service delivery, or arm’s-length pricing, or the WFOE deliberately under-reports PRC-source income by having clients remit directly to the Taiwan parent’s offshore bank account while the WFOE books only a nominal service fee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 41 and Article 47, the STA may apply the GAAR and make a transfer pricing adjustment, add the under-reported income to taxable profits, and levy a deficiency interest surcharge; under Tax Administration Law Article 63, evasion of EIT exceeding RMB 50,000 triggers an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax, confiscation of illegal gains, and blacklisting of the enterprise; a criminal referral is mandatory if the evaded amount exceeds 30% of the taxable income for a single year and is over RMB 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and financial supervisor of the WFOE may be personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax plus the 0.05% daily surcharge and the penalty; if the enterprise is a mere conduit or shell, the court may pierce the corporate veil and hold the Taiwan parent and its directors jointly and severally liable for the WFOE’s tax debts; on criminal conviction, directors, financial officers, and tax-return preparers face up to 7 years’ imprisonment and fines for tax evasion, and may be subjected to a departure ban (出境限制) and a blacklist preventing them from serving as directors of any Chinese enterprise for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Phony Transfer Pricing Documentation / Thin Capitalization / Round-Tripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE files an annual related-party transaction form with false or incomplete disclosure of intercompany loans, IP royalties, or service fees, or uses a 100% shareholder loan without a written agreement and an interest rate above the People’s Bank of China benchmark, or routes payments through Hong Kong or Singapore shell companies to disguise a Taiwan parent dividend as a tax-deductible royalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 114 of the Tax Administration Law and Notice 2017 No. 6 (STA TP Management Measures) allow the STA to disregard the transaction, recharacterize the debt as equity, apply the 2:1 thin capitalization ratio, disallow the excessive interest expense, and deem the payment a dividend subject to 10% WHT plus VAT; a late or incorrect related-party form is punishable by a penalty of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000; the underpaid tax is subject to a 5-year limitation period if there is reasonable disclosure, but if concealment is proven, the limitation period is extended to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the compliance certificate certifying false transfer pricing documentation are personally exposed to criminal liability for tax fraud; if the WFOE cannot pay the assessed tax, the tax authority may impose a property preservation order freezing bank accounts and real estate of the legal representative and the beneficial owners, and may limit the legal representative’s exit; a Hong Kong or Taiwan court may order directors to restore misappropriated payments to the WFOE’s estate in a shareholder derivative action, and personal bankruptcy proceedings can be triggered by the restitution order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failing to Withhold and Pay WHT on Cross-Border Dividends, Interest, or Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE remits dividends to the Taiwan parent (or pays interest/royalties to a Taiwan licensor) without withholding 10% (or 5% treaty rate if applicable) EIT, fails to file the withholding return, and does not report the payment in the annual related-party transaction schedule; additionally, the WFOE fails to obtain the Taiwan parent’s Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration, or allows the Taiwan parent to claim treaty relief without satisfying the 365-day shareholding requirement by distributing within the first year of capital injection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Administration Law Article 69, a withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit the required tax is liable for the tax itself plus a 50% to 300% penalty on the unwithheld amount; if the WFOE fails to file the withholding return on time, a separate penalty of RMB 2,000 plus RMB 2,000 per day up to RMB 20,000 applies; interest at 0.05% per day accumulates from the due date until payment; if the Taiwan parent is found not to be the beneficial owner and the treaty relief is revoked, the WFOE becomes jointly liable for the full 10% WHT plus penalty and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and chief financial officer are civilly liable for the withheld tax under the enterprise liability rules and may have personal assets attached if they knowingly signed remittance instructions that ignored the withholding obligation; a criminal conviction for failure to withhold exceeding RMB 100,000 can result in up to 3 years’ imprisonment, while any additional false statement of a tax officer can trigger the separate offense of tax fraud with a sentence of up to 7 years; departure bans are routinely imposed on the legal representative of a WFOE that has a significant uncollected withholding tax liability.
